messages:
maya: FYI rolling kernel-selector v4 this morning and we're getting a host CPU uplift on some edge pools. quick pprof points at http2 frame parse -> grpc header decode -> pretokenize scan. also lots of small writev syscalls.

leo: can you paste the flame? wondering if batch hints changed.

maya: ```
28.0%  http2_frame_read
19.0%  grpc_decode_headers
13.5%  pretokenize_scan
9.0%   kvcache.lookup
6.7%   writev (many <512B iovecs)
```

maya: observed writev per-worker jumped 100/s -> ~420/s, p99 latency +35ms on affected hosts.

sam: traffic slice? looks like mobile api and websocket proxy paths. v4 changed kernel selection to prefer short-sequence optimized kernels when seqlen_hint < 64. that could reduce model cost but increase host-side fragmentation.

jess: kv miss rate on those hosts went 3.8% -> 8.5%. raw: lookups 1,000,000 misses 85k.

jess: ```
kv_lookup_total: 1000000
kv_lookup_miss: 85000 # 8.5%
kv_lookup_prev_miss: 38000 # 3.8%
```

kai: likely two compounding effects: selector chooses kernel variant that changes kv key stride/alignment -> kv thrash; and smaller minibatches -> more frequent partial token emission -> frame assembler flushes small frames -> writev spike.

leo: short-term mitigations: 1) ingress coalesce shim (buffer up to 2KB or 5ms), 2) runtime writev aggregator to merge small iovecs before syscall, 3) bias selector config to prefer previous kernel on mobile hostpools.

sam: small experiment: rolled a 5% canary reverting selector to previous kernel on hostgroup=edge-canary. early 15m telemetry: canary hosts show CPU -6% and writev -60% vs v4.

maya: good signal. can we get owners for fixes? leo -> runtime writev-agg PR, jess + sam -> ingress coalesce shim, kai -> perf-ci microbench for header+fragment combinations. I'll open a tracking issue.

leo: I'll draft the writev aggregator tonight. low-risk change: coalesce adjacent iovecs under 512B into a single syscall buffer; feature-flagged.

jess: sam and I will pair on a tiny rust sidecar that coalesces inbound fragments (time+size) before forwarding. feature-flag behind ff and opt-in hostgroups.

kai: adding a microbench to perf-ci: generator emits header+payload in 64/128/256/512B fragments; run across kernels and measure parse CPU, kv-miss, writev_count. also adding a unit test asserting typical mobile request has <=8 writev iovs.

sre-bot: created incident INC-2026-046 (host-parse-writev-uplift) linked to thread 6561112222

maya: plan: land writev-agg to canary within 6h, coalesce shim draft in ~4h. tracker INF-2481 created. will post canary dashboards here.

leo: will include microbench results in PR and a simple benchmark script.

maya: thanks everyone. if canary holds we'll roll bias config back to selector after tests. otherwise auto-gate will flip.
